pages.title: MAINTAIN AI — Project Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to MAINTAIN AI: what it is, its architecture (FastAPI backend + React frontend + Electron desktop wrapper), key capabilities, and how the three sub-projects fit together. Links to child pages for setup and architecture details.

pages.title: Getting Started & Setup
pages.purpose: Step-by-step guide for running MAINTAIN AI locally: prerequisites (Python 3.10+, Node 18+), installing backend dependencies, seeding demo data, starting the FastAPI server, starting the Vite dev server, and optionally enabling the Gemini AI path. Covers troubleshooting common startup errors.

pages.title: Repository Structure
pages.purpose: Explains the monorepo layout: backend/, frontend/, desktop/, and .github/ directories, what each contains, and how they relate. Describes the build artifact flow (frontend/dist and backend/dist consumed by the desktop Electron wrapper).

pages.title: Backend Architecture
pages.purpose: Overview of the FastAPI backend: application entry point, middleware, router registration, database initialization, and the SQLite persistence layer. Links to child pages covering data models, API routers, and the alerts engine.

pages.title: Data Models & Schemas
pages.purpose: Detailed reference for all SQLAlchemy ORM models (Machine, Component, FaultRecord, SensorReading, MaintenanceRecord, WorkOrder, Alert, SparePart, KnowledgeBaseEntry, AIDiagnosticSession, User, AppSetting) and their Pydantic schema counterparts. Covers enums (HealthStatus, Priority, WorkOrderStatus, etc.), relationships, and cascade rules.

pages.title: API Routers
pages.purpose: Reference for all nine FastAPI routers: machines, maintenance, work_orders, alerts, spare_parts, ai_assistant, reports, users, and settings. Documents each router's prefix, key endpoints (CRUD operations, status transitions, sub-resources), and notable business logic (e.g., completing a work order auto-creates a MaintenanceRecord).

pages.title: Smart Alert Engine
pages.purpose: Deep dive into alerts_engine.py: how evaluate_all() and evaluate_machine() work, the three alert triggers (low health score, maintenance overdue/due-soon, repeated unresolved faults), deduplication via raise_alert(), AlertSeverity levels, and how the engine is invoked.

pages.title: Reporting & Data Export
pages.purpose: Covers the reports router and export sub-system: dashboard summary endpoint, reliability report, failure analysis, recent-faults and recent-activity feeds, and the three export formats (CSV via stdlib, PDF via ReportLab, Excel via openpyxl). Explains the build_pdf_report and build_excel_report functions.

pages.title: AI Diagnostic System
pages.purpose: Overview of the two-tier AI diagnostic architecture: offline-first engine with Gemini cloud fallback. Explains the POST /api/ai/diagnose flow, AIDiagnosticSession persistence, and the outcome feedback loop. Links to child pages for each engine.

pages.title: Offline Diagnostic Engine
pages.purpose: Detailed explanation of offline_engine.py: knowledge_base.json structure (machine_category, symptoms, causes with confidence scores, clarifying questions, recommended_procedure), the symptom-scoring algorithm (_score_entry), certainty labelling (_certainty_label), the iterative question-answer loop, and PyInstaller frozen-binary path resolution for knowledge_base.json.

pages.title: Gemini Cloud Integration
pages.purpose: Documents gemini_client.py: the diagnose_with_gemini() function, _resolve_api_key() priority logic (DB setting → env var), SYSTEM_INSTRUCTION prompt engineering, the strict JSON response schema, model configuration (gemini-3.5-flash, GEMINI_MODEL env var), and the silent-failure/fallback design. Covers the AppSetting key storage pattern and the Settings UI for key management.

pages.title: Frontend Application
pages.purpose: Overview of the React/Vite frontend: application shell (App.jsx), routing structure, sidebar navigation, LiquidGlass UI library integration, FPSGuard performance management, theme toggling, and the API client. Links to child pages for pages and components.

pages.title: Pages & Navigation
pages.purpose: Documents each of the ten frontend pages: Dashboard (summary tiles, charts, recent activity), Machines (list + MachineDetail with sensor readings and components), Maintenance (schedule management), WorkOrders (Kanban-style board), AIAssistant (interactive diagnosis UI), Alerts, SpareParts, Reports (with export buttons), and Settings. Covers the PageHeaderContext pattern for dynamic page titles.

pages.title: Shared Components & Styling
pages.purpose: Covers reusable UI building blocks: StatusBadge (maps health/severity strings to coloured badges), Charts.jsx (HealthDistributionChart pie, MachineHealthBarChart, GenericBarChart using Recharts), index.css design tokens (CSS variables for colours, stat-grid, LiquidGlass panel classes), and the LiquidGlass/@sohumsuthar/liquid-glass library usage patterns.

pages.title: Desktop Application (Electron)
pages.purpose: Overview of the Electron wrapper: how main.js orchestrates backend process spawning, the waitForServer health-check loop, BrowserWindow creation, dev vs. packaged mode differences, per-user database path (app.getPath('userData')), and graceful shutdown. Links to child pages for build configuration and CI/CD.

pages.title: Desktop Build & Packaging
pages.purpose: Explains the electron-builder configuration in desktop/package.json: extraResources mapping (backend/dist → backend/, frontend/dist → frontend/), platform targets (NSIS for Windows, DMG for macOS, AppImage+deb for Linux), appId, and the npm run dev / npm run dist scripts. Covers the PyInstaller .spec file for bundling the Python backend.

pages.title: CI/CD Pipeline
pages.purpose: Documents the GitHub Actions build-desktop.yml workflow: trigger conditions (push v* tags, workflow_dispatch), the three-OS matrix (windows-latest, macos-latest, ubuntu-latest), the sequential build stages (frontend Vite build with VITE_API_URL injection → PyInstaller backend packaging → electron-builder distribution), artifact upload strategy, and npm caching.

pages.title: Seed Data & Demo Environment
pages.purpose: Explains seed_data.py: the eight pre-configured machines (induction motors, pumps, conveyors, compressors), seeded fault records, maintenance history, work orders, spare parts, users, and AI diagnostic sessions. Describes how to run seeding, reset the database, and how evaluate_all() is called at the end of seeding to generate initial alerts.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.purpose: Definitions of all codebase-specific terms, domain concepts, abbreviations, and jargon that an onboarding engineer needs to know, each with code pointers.

pages.title: Project Credits & Authors
pages.purpose: Credits and authorship information for the MAINTAIN AI project, identifying the contributors responsible for the project.

page_notes.content: MAINTAIN AI was created by Durvesh M. Jadhav, Shrikant K. Katkar, and Viraj V. Patil.
